question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes respectively. If both pipes are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the tank?
explanation: Rate of pipe A = 1/20. Rate of pipe B = 1/30. Combined rate = 1/20 + 1/30 = 5/60 = 1/12. Time = 12 minutes.
formulaUsed: Time = (A × B) / (A + B) for two filling pipes

question: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours. Due to a leak at the bottom, it is filled in 20 hours. If the tank is full, how long will the leak take to empty it?
explanation: Rate of filling pipe = 1/15. Net rate with leak = 1/20. Leak rate = 1/15 - 1/20 = (4-3)/60 = 1/60. Leak empties tank in 60 hours.
formulaUsed: Leak Rate = Fill Rate - Net Rate

question: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 minutes and pipe B fills it in 18 minutes. Pipe C empties it in 36 minutes. If all three are opened, how long to fill the tank?
shortcutMethod: LCM = 36. A = 3 units, B = 2 units, C = -1 unit. Net = 4 units/min. Time = 36/4 = 9 min.
formulaUsed: Net Rate = Sum of fill rates - Sum of drain rates
